arxiv-2008-12725.title: iviz: A ROS Visualization App for Mobile Devices
arxiv-2008-12725.creator: Antonio Zea and Uwe D. Hanebeck
arxiv-2008-12725.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Antonio Zea and Uwe D. Hanebeck. In this work, we introduce iviz , a mobile application for visualizing ROS data. In the last few years, the popularity of ROS has grown enormously, making it the standard platform for open source robotic programming. A key reason for this success is the availability of polished, general-purpose modules for many tasks, such as localization, mapping, path planning, and quite importantly, data visualization.

arxiv-2012-14933.title: Surprise Maximization: A Dynamic Programming Approach
arxiv-2012-14933.creator: Ali Eshragh
arxiv-2012-14933.description: Abstract Borwein et al. [ 1 ] solved a “surprise maximization” problem by applying results from convex analysis and mathematical programming. Although, their proof is elegant, it requires advanced knowledge from both areas to understand it. Here, we provide another approach to derive an optimal solution of the problem by utilizing dynamic programming. \mdtheorem [style=theoremstyle]claimClaim 1 Introduction Borwein et al.

arxiv-2105-00281.title: Rational and p p -adic analogs of J.H.C. Whitehead’s conjecture
arxiv-2105-00281.creator: A. M. Mikhovich
arxiv-2105-00281.description: Abstract We show that subpresentations of aspherical prounipotent presentations over fields of zero characteristics and subpresentations of aspherical pro- p p -presentations are aspherical; an application to subpresentations of aspherical discrete presentations is also included. Following Bousfield-Kan, Quillen and Sullivan the results are regarded as affirmative answers to rational and p p -adic analogs of J.H.C. Whitehead’s conjecture.

arxiv-2204-05899.title: VisCUIT : Visual Auditor for Bias in CNN Image Classifier
arxiv-2204-05899.creator: Seongmin Lee, Zijie J. Wang, Judy Hoffman, Duen Horng (Polo) Chau
arxiv-2204-05899.description: Abstract CNN image classifiers are widely used, thanks to their efficiency and accuracy. However, they can suffer from biases that impede their practical applications. Most existing bias investigation techniques are either inapplicable to general image classification tasks or require significant user efforts in perusing all data subgroups to manually specify which data attributes to inspect.

arxiv-2302-14582.title: ManQala: Game-Inspired Strategies for Quantum State Engineering
arxiv-2302-14582.creator: Onur Danaci, Wenlei Zhang, Robert Coleman, William Djakam, Michaela Amoo, Ryan T. Glasser, Brian T. Kirby, Moussa N’Gom, Thomas A. Searles
arxiv-2302-14582.description: Abstract The ability to prepare systems in specific target states through quantum engineering is essential for realizing the new technologies promised by a second quantum revolution. Here, we recast the fundamental problem of state preparation in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces as ManQala, a quantum game inspired by the West African sowing game mancala.

arxiv-2303-05453.title: Personalisation within bounds : A risk taxonomy and policy framework for the alignment of large language models with personalised feedback
arxiv-2303-05453.creator: Hannah Rose Kirk, Bertie Vidgen, Paul Röttger, Scott A. Hale
arxiv-2303-05453.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are used to generate content for an increasingly wide range of tasks, and are set to reach a growing audience in coming years due to integration in product interfaces like ChatGPT or search engines like Bing.

arxiv-2305-18646.title: Deep Equilibrium Models Meet Federated Learning This work was supported in part by the University of Patras and the RPF, Cyprus, under the project INFRASTRUCTURES/1216/0017 (IRIDA).
arxiv-2305-18646.creator: Alexandros Gkillas 1 , Dimitris Ampeliotis 2 , Kostas Berberidis 1
arxiv-2305-18646.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Alexandros Gkillas 1 , Dimitris Ampeliotis 2 , Kostas Berberidis 1. In this study the problem of Federated Learning (FL) is explored under a new perspective by utilizing the Deep Equilibrium (DEQ) models instead of conventional deep learning networks. We claim that incorporating DEQ models into the federated learning framework naturally addresses several open problems in FL, such as the communication overhead due to the sharing large models and the ability to incorporate heterogeneous edge devices with significantly different computation capabilities.

arxiv-2312-03989.title: Rapid detection of rare events from in situ X-ray diffraction data using machine learning
arxiv-2312-03989.creator: Weijian Zheng, † Jun-Sang Park, † Peter Kenesei, Ahsan Ali, Zhengchun Liu, Ian T. Foster, Nicholas Schwarz, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Antonino Miceli, Hemant Sharma ∗ Argonne National Laboratory, 9700 S Cass Ave, Lemont, IL, USA ∗ To whom correspondence should be addressed: hsharma@anl.gov † Equal contri
arxiv-2312-03989.description: Abstract High-energy X-ray diffraction methods can non-destructively map the 3D microstructure and associated attributes of metallic polycrystalline engineering materials in their bulk form. These methods are often combined with external stimuli such as thermo-mechanical loading to take snapshots over time of the evolving microstructure and attributes.

arxiv-2312-13056.title: Lightcone fluctuations in a five dimensional Kaluza-Klein model and an estimation on the size of the extra dimension
arxiv-2312-13056.creator: 1 Giulia Aleixo, 1 Herondy Mota
arxiv-2312-13056.description: Abstract In this work we consider lightcone fluctuation effects in a five-dimensional spacetime arising as a consequence of the compactification of the extra dimension via a quasiperiodic condition, characterized by a phase angle 2 ​ π ​ α 2\pi\alpha .

arxiv-2402-02689.title: Planar Graphs with Homomorphisms to the 9-cycle
arxiv-2402-02689.creator: Daniel W. Cranston, Jiaao Li, Zhouningxin Wang, Chunyan Wei
arxiv-2402-02689.description: Abstract We study the problem of finding homomorphisms into odd cycles from planar graphs with high odd-girth. The Jaeger-Zhang conjecture states that every planar graph of odd-girth at least 4 ​ k + 1 4k+1 admits a homomorphism to the odd cycle C 2 ​ k + 1 C_{2k+1} .

arxiv-2407-08765.title: Approximating G ⁡ ( t ) / G ​ I / 1 G(t)/GI/1 queues with deep learning
arxiv-2407-08765.creator: Eliran Sherzer, Opher Baron, Dmitry Krass, Yehezkel Resheff
arxiv-2407-08765.description: Abstract Many real-world queueing systems exhibit a time-dependent arrival process and can be modeled as a G ⁡ ( t ) / G ​ I / 1 G(t)/GI/1 queue. Despite its wide applicability, little can be derived analytically about this system, particularly its transient behavior.

arxiv-2407-09317.title: Bonding states underpinning structural transitions in IrTe 2 observed with micro-ARPES
arxiv-2407-09317.creator: C. W. Nicholson, M. D. Watson, A. Pulkkinen, M. Rumo, G. Kremer, K. Y. Ma, F. O. von Rohr, C. Cacho, C. Monney
arxiv-2407-09317.description: Abstract Competing interactions in low-dimensional materials can produce nearly degenerate electronic and structural phases. We investigate the staircase of structural phase transitions in layered IrTe 2 for which a number of potential transition mechanisms have been postulated. The spatial coexistence of multiple phases on the micron scale has prevented a detailed analysis of the electronic structure.

arxiv-2409-09085.title: HESSO: Towards Automatic Efficient and User Friendly Any Neural Network Training and Pruning
arxiv-2409-09085.creator: Tianyi Chen *, Xiaoyi Qu, David Aponte, Colby Banbury, Jongwoo Ko
arxiv-2409-09085.description: Abstract Structured pruning is a popular technique for compressing deep neural networks (DNNs) into efficient sub-networks. However, existing methods often require multi-stage process, engineering efforts, and human expertise. The Only-Train-Once series (OTOv1-v3) has been proposed to resolve some pain points by streamlining the workflow.

arxiv-2410-15518.title: TrackMe: A Simple and Effective Multiple Object Tracking Annotation Tool
arxiv-2410-15518.creator: Thinh Phan, Isaac Phillips, Andrew Lockett, Michael T.Kidd, Ngan Le
arxiv-2410-15518.description: Abstract Object tracking, especially animal tracking, is one of the key topics that attract a lot of attention due to its benefits of animal behavior understanding and monitoring. Recent state-of-the-art tracking methods are founded on deep learning architectures for object detection, appearance feature extraction and track association.

arxiv-2412-15620.title: Modeling Autonomous Shifts Between Focus State and Mind-Wandering Using a Predictive-Coding-Inspired Variational RNN Model
arxiv-2412-15620.creator: Henrique Oyama, Jun Tani
arxiv-2412-15620.description: Abstract The current study investigates possible neural mechanisms underling autonomous shifts between focus state and mind-wandering by conducting model simulation experiments. On this purpose, we modeled perception processes of continuous sensory sequences using our previous proposed variational RNN model which was developed based on the free energy principle.

arxiv-2501-00573.title: Exploring Quantum-Dot Engineered Solid-State Photon Upconversion in PbS:Yb 3+ ,Er 3+ /CuBiO Using Density Functional Theory and Machine Learning Methods for Water Splitting
arxiv-2501-00573.creator: Dennis Delali Kwesi Wayo, Vladislav Kudryashov, Mirat Karibayev, Gertrude Ellen Fynn, Khadichakhan Rafikova, Camila Martins Saporetti, Leonardo Goliatt, Nurxat Nuraje
arxiv-2501-00573.description: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive numerical analysis of a quantum-dot-engineered heterostructure, PbS:Yb 3+ ,Er 3+ /CuBiO, optimized for water splitting applications. Using density functional theory (DFT) coupled with machine learning, the study explores the electronic, optical, and catalytic properties of the material. The optimized PbS structure exhibited a direct bandgap of 1.

arxiv-2503-10699.title: Test-Time Discovery via Hashing Memory Thanks: Equal contributions.
arxiv-2503-10699.creator: Fan Lyu, Tianle Liu, Zhang Zhang, Fuyuan Hu, Liang Wang
arxiv-2503-10699.description: Abstract We introduce Test-Time Discovery (TTD) as a novel task that addresses class shifts during testing, requiring models to simultaneously identify emerging categories while preserving previously learned ones. A key challenge in TTD is distinguishing newly discovered classes from those already identified.

arxiv-2507-15443.title: Evaluating Joint Attention for Mixed-Presence Collaboration on Wall-Sized Displays Conference: Companion Proceedings of the 17th ACM SIGCHI Symposium on Engineering Interactive Computing Systems; June 23–27, 2025; Trier, Germany Companion Proceedings of the 17th ACM SIGCHI Symposium on Engineering I

arxiv-2507-15443.description: Abstract . To understand and quantify the quality of mixed-presence collaboration around wall-sized displays, robust evaluation methodologies are needed, that are adapted for a room-sized experience and are not perceived as obtrusive. In this paper, we propose our approach for measuring joint attention based on head gaze data.

arxiv-2509-09004.title: Implicit Neural Representations of Intramyocardial Motion and Strain
arxiv-2509-09004.creator: Andrew Bell, Yan Kit Choi, Steffen E Petersen, Andrew King, Muhummad Sohaib Nazir, Alistair A Young
arxiv-2509-09004.description: Abstract Automatic quantification of intramyocardial motion and strain from tagging MRI remains an important but challenging task. We propose a method using implicit neural representations (INRs), conditioned on learned latent codes, to predict continuous left ventricular (LV) displacement — without requiring inference-time optimisation. Evaluated on 452 UK Biobank test cases, our method achieved the best tracking accuracy (2.

arxiv-2510-11638.creator: Yijia Fang, Gennian Ge, Yang Shu, Qian Xu, Zixiang Xu, Dilong Yang

arxiv-2512-00946.title: Fine-tuning of lightweight large language models for sentiment classification on heterogeneous financial textual data Journal: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence
arxiv-2512-00946.creator: Alvaro Paredes Amorin, Andre Python, Christoph Weisser
arxiv-2512-00946.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) play an increasingly important role in financial markets analysis by capturing signals from complex and heterogeneous textual data sources, such as tweets, news articles, reports, and microblogs. However, their performance is dependent on large computational resources and proprietary datasets, which are costly, restricted, and therefore inaccessible to many researchers and practitioners.

arxiv-2512-02474.title: Q-BERT4Rec: Quantized Semantic-ID Representation Learning for Multimodal Recommendation DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation email; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 Thanks: * Corresponding author
arxiv-2512-02474.creator: Haofeng Huang 1, Ling Gai 2,*
arxiv-2512-02474.description: Abstract . Sequential recommendation plays a critical role in modern online platforms such as e-commerce, advertising, and content streaming, where accurately predicting users’ next interactions is essential for personalization. Recent Transformer-based methods like BERT4Rec have shown strong modeling capability, yet they still rely on discrete item IDs that lack semantic meaning and ignore rich multimodal information (e.g., text and image).

arxiv-2512-15777.title: Variable Record Table: A Unified Hardware-Assisted Framework for Runtime Security
arxiv-2512-15777.creator: Suraj Kumar Sah, Love Kumar Sah
arxiv-2512-15777.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Suraj Kumar Sah, Love Kumar Sah. Modern computing systems face security threats, including memory corruption attacks, speculative execution vulnerabilities, and control-flow hijacking. Although existing solutions address these threats individually, they frequently introduce performance overhead and leave security gaps. This paper presents a Variable Record Table (VRT) with a unified hardware-assisted framework that simultaneously enforces spatial memory safety against buffer overflows, back-edge control-flow integrity (CFI), and speculative execution attack detection.

pmc-10721991.title: Correlation of brain iron deposition and freezing of gait in Parkinson’s disease: a cross-sectional study
pmc-10721991.creator: Ying Yan, Zheng Wang, Wei Wei, Zhenghan Yang, Lingfei Guo, Zhenchang Wang, Xuan Wei
pmc-10721991.description: BackgroundQuantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) is a novel imaging method for detecting iron content in the brain. The study aimed determine whether the iron deposition in the brains of people with Parkinson’s disease (PD) is correlated with freezing of gait (FOG).

pmc-11282077.title: KPNA2 promotes the progression of gastric cancer by regulating the alternative splicing of related genes
pmc-11282077.creator: Xia Chen, Hui Wei, Ailin Yue, Huiyun Zhang, Ya Zheng, Weiming Sun, Yongning Zhou, Yuping Wang
pmc-11282077.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) play critical roles in genome regulation. In this study, we explored the latent function of KPNA2, which is an essential member of the RBP family, in the regulation of alternative splicing (AS) in gastric cancer (GC). We analyzed the role of KPNA2 in regulating differential expression and AS via RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and improved RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (iRIP-seq). Clinical specimens were used to analyze the associations between KPNA2 expression and clinicopathological characteristics.

pmc-11410560.title: Variation in parental investment preferences for nestlings of the Gray‐backed Shrike (Lanius tephronotus) in alpine environments
pmc-11410560.creator: Jinyuan Zeng, Yueqi Li, Yuhan Gong, Yurou Shi, Hongyuan Feng, Sen Song
pmc-11410560.description: In the northeastern edge of the Qinghai‐Tibet Plateau, the Gray‐backed Shrike, a shrubland bird species of the plateau, confronts harsh living conditions. The impact of such an environment on their reproductive strategies has long intrigued us. This study reveals significant environmental effects on the investment of the Gray‐backed Shrike during their nestling‐rearing and egg‐laying stages.

pmc-11529826.title: Income in Relation to Psychosocial Factors Among Stroke Survivors using Smartwatches for Atrial Fibrillation Monitoring
pmc-11529826.creator: Syed Naeem, Tyler Jones, Joseph Daniel, Jordy Mehawej, Andreas Filippaios, Tenes Paul, Ziyue Wang, Sakeina Howard-Wilson, Darleen Lessard, Eric Ding, Edith Mensah Otabil, Kamran Noorishirazi, Apurv Soni, Jane Saczynski, Khanh-Van Tran, David McManus
pmc-11529826.description: Background:Timely detection of atrial fibrillation (AF) is critical for stroke prevention. Smartwatches are FDA-approved devices that can now aide in this detection.Objective:Investigate how socioeconomic status is associated with self-reported psychosocial outcomes, including anxiety, patient activation, and health-related quality of life in stroke survivors using smartwatch for AF detection.Methods:We analyzed data from the Pulsewatch study, a randomized controlled trial (NCT03761394).

pmc-11617798.title: Psychopathy checklist‐youth version scores and recurring victimisation by an intimate partner in a justice‐involved sample: A comparison of young men and women using longitudinal data
pmc-11617798.creator: Michelle N. Harris, Leah E. Daigle, Dennis Reidy, Travis Chafin, Nick D. Thomson
pmc-11617798.description: BackgroundPeople involved in the criminal justice system are at increased risk of recurring intimate partner violent (IPV) victimisation. Experience of trauma is linked to a variety of negative outcomes, including repeated experiences, so it is important to identify factors that may distinguish non‐victims, single‐event victims and recurring victims at an early stage as this could hold potential for intervention efforts.

pmc-12403383.title: Anxiety, depression and fear of disease progression among Chinese parents of children with retinoblastoma
pmc-12403383.creator: Yilin Yu, Yiyi Feng, Yanping Han, Jie Yang, Xuyang Wen, Xianqun Fan, Jiayan Fan
pmc-12403383.description: BackgroundRecent studies indicate parents of childhood cancer survivors experience high psychological burden. However, there is limited knowledge regarding the mental health of parents of children with retinoblastoma (RB) in China. Thus, the purpose of this study was to assess anxiety, depression, fear of disease progression (FoP), and family function among parents of children with RB, and to analyze associated factors.

pmc-12428348.title: Development and Application of a Novel pH-Responsive Bilayer Indicator Film for Yellowfin Seabream Preservation and Freshness Monitoring
pmc-12428348.creator: Shan Xue, Zhi Lin, Jia Liu, Young-Teck Kim
pmc-12428348.description: A pH-responsive bilayer film was developed for real-time freshness monitoring and preservation of yellowfin seabream. The emulsified layer contained chitosan (CS) and flaxseed oil (FO), while the indicator layer comprised carrageenan (CAR), gelatin (GEL), grape seed anthocyanins (GSA), and curcumin (CUR). Optimization via response surface methodology determined the ideal formulation: CAR/GEL mass ratio 1.11:1, CS concentration 1.

pmc-13214731.title: Brain-First vs. Body-First Models in Neurodegenerative Disease: A Perspective Review
pmc-13214731.creator: Giuseppe Forte, Maria Casagrande
pmc-13214731.description: Recent advances in neurodegenerative disease research increasingly support the existence of multiple trajectory signatures underlying the heterogeneity of cognitive decline syndromes. Originally proposed in Parkinson’s disease, the brain-first and body-first models have emerged as conceptual frameworks to explain variability in disease onset, prodromal features, and progression across dementia-related disorders.

pmc-13374396.title: Impact of vitamin D levels on disease activity, function and health over 2 years in radiographic axial spondyloarthritis: data from GErman SPondyloarthritis Inception Cohort (GESPIC)
pmc-13374396.creator: Murat Torgutalp, Fabian Proft, Hildrun Haibel, Henriette Baum, Marina D’Urso, Caroline Höppner, Mikhail Protopopov, Judith Rademacher, Didem Sahin, Denis Poddubnyy, Valeria Rios Rodriguez
pmc-13374396.description: ObjectivesTo investigate the impact of vitamin D on disease activity, function and health in patients with radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA) undergoing biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (bDMARD) therapy.MethodsPatients with r-axSpA and active disease at baseline initiating a bDMARD were included in this analysis.

pmc-13389499.title: Maternal control during prenatal oxycodone exposure: differential effects of voluntary versus involuntary self-administration on offspring substance use vulnerability in rats
pmc-13389499.creator: Chantal CA Aaron, Kerri E. Budge, Sara B. Isgate, Fair M. Vassoler, Elizabeth M. Byrnes
pmc-13389499.description: Prenatal opioid exposure is a growing clinical concern, yet the impact of maternal control over drug intake on long-term offspring outcomes remains unclear. Here, we utilized a translational rat model to examine how the mode of oxycodone administration during pregnancy influences substance use vulnerability in adult offspring.

pmc-13562142.title: Early versus late closure of protective ileostomy after rectal cancer surgery
pmc-13562142.creator: Elias Khajeh, Andrea Sosková, Johanna Fellhofer-Hofer, Nastaran Sabetkish, Rajan Nikbakhsh, Mohammadamin Shahrbaf, Arianeb Mehrabi, Fee Klupp
pmc-13562142.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeThe optimal timing of protective ileostomy closure after rectal cancer surgery remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis compares early (EC) versus late closure (LC) and evaluates the associated risks and benefits.MethodsMedline, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched for RCTs published up to May 2025 that compared EC (≤ 30 days after creation) with LC (≥ 12 weeks after creation) following rectal cancer surgery.ResultsNine RCTs including 387 patients (EC: 195, LC: 192) were analyzed.
